findings.title: Null check in AccessTokenContext constructor checks grantType instead of rawTokenId
findings.body: In the `AccessTokenContext` constructor, line 73 calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` instead of checking `rawTokenId`. As a result, a null `rawTokenId` is accepted without throwing a `NullPointerException`, violating the constructor's intended invariant.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher uses wrong substring indices and inverted equality check
findings.body: In `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId`, the prefix before `:` is 6 characters long (`<2-char sessionType><2-char tokenType><2-char grantType>`, e.g., `onrtac`), so the grant shortcut is at `substring(4, 6)` rather than `substring(3, 5)`. Furthermore, the condition `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` is inverted (missing `!`). Because `substring(3, 5)` extracts the second character of the token type plus the first character of the grant type (e.g., `ta`), it never equals `expectedGrantShortcut`, causing the matcher to accidentally pass without ever verifying the grant shortcut (and it would throw `IndexOutOfBoundsException` if `items[0]` has fewer than 5 characters).

findings.title: Javadoc for getShortcut() says 3-letters shortcut, but encoder requires exactly 2 characters
findings.body: The Javadoc on `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` states `@return usually like 3-letters shortcut of specific grants`. However, all implementations return 2-character shortcuts and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId` strictly requires the encoded context to be 6 characters total (`encodedContext.length() != 6`) and extracts the grant shortcut via `encodedContext.substring(4, 6)`. Implementing a 3-letter shortcut as suggested by the Javadoc will cause token ID decoding to fail with an `IllegalArgumentException`.
